curriculum_title: Enterprise Agentic AI & World Models Study Map
target_audience: Medium-to-large professional services firms and enterprises
framework_orientation: Foundation & World Models at bottom bedrock layer, escalating to Agentic Harness, Data Layers, and Enterprise Client Deliverables

playlists.name: Phase 0: Non-IT Professional Enablement & Confidence with AI
playlists.subtitle: Executive Judgment, Safe Prompting & De-Risking AI for Non-Technical Leaders
playlists.target_role: Managing Partners, Practice Heads, Directors & Non-Technical Executives
playlists.description: A tailored masterclass series designed specifically for legal partners, accountants, and practice heads. Learn how to direct, evaluate, and supervise AI as an executive associate without writing code, maintain strict client privilege, and ask your MSP the hard questions.
playlists.vendor_note: Professional services firms do not need an internal army of data scientists, but leaders must possess AI fluency. Ask your managed service provider (MSP) and software vendors how client confidentiality boundaries and zero-retention policies are enforced across daily office tools.

videos.title: AI Risk for Leadership: Closing the Executive Disconnect
videos.summary: Sushila Nair breaks down executive liability, board governance, and the widening chasm between rapid staff AI adoption and formal security protocols.
videos.jargon_explained: Human-in-the-Loop Supervision is a governance term for ensuring a qualified human professional actively reviews, verifies, and signs off on every AI-assisted deliverable before it reaches a client or regulator.
vendor_questions: Ask your firm's managing committee whether partners have personal sign-off liability for work assisted by third-party AI.
Ask your managed service provider (MSP) which AI tools are currently active across your firm's workstations without formal management approval.

videos.title: What is Shadow AI? The Dark Horse of Cybersecurity Threats
videos.summary: Analyzes how employees unknowingly compromise confidential client data by pasting sensitive text into unvetted consumer AI tools, and how leaders can establish safe corporate guardrails.
videos.jargon_explained: Shadow AI is an operational risk term for the unauthorized use of consumer AI software by staff to complete work tasks without IT review, creating unmonitored data exfiltration risks.
vendor_questions: Ask the person responsible for your IT what technological measures prevent staff from pasting privileged client files into public web-based chatbots.
Ask your software vendors whether enterprise licenses guarantee that client prompt data is completely excluded from public model training.

videos.title: RAG vs Fine-Tuning vs Prompt Engineering: Optimizing AI Without Coding
videos.summary: Demystifies the three main ways organizations tailor AI models. Translates technical buzzwords into clear business choices: instructing an AI (prompting), connecting it to internal firm files (RAG), or retraining it (fine-tuning).
videos.jargon_explained: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is an enterprise AI term for connecting an AI model directly to your firm's approved internal documents, allowing it to cite real firm precedents without hallucinating.
vendor_questions: Ask your software vendors whether their 'AI solution' is merely sending prompts to a public model or securely searching your firm's own indexed document repository.
Ask the person responsible for IT procurement how vendor contracts protect your firm's intellectual property when connecting internal document drives to AI retrieval systems.

videos.title: AI in the Crosshairs: Threat Modeling for Professional Services
videos.summary: A deep dive into systemic AI vulnerabilities, threat modeling for professional advisory firms, and establishing an independent risk baseline.
videos.jargon_explained: Threat Modeling is a risk management term for systematically identifying potential vulnerabilities, attack vectors, and operational failure points in your AI workflows before they cause a breach.
vendor_questions: Ask your managed service provider (MSP) what incident response protocols exist if an AI tool leaks confidential client communication.
Ask your compliance officer what independent audit trail exists to reconstruct how an AI-assisted recommendation was formulated.

videos.title: The Importance of AI Governance: From Principles to Practice
videos.summary: Explains how forward-thinking leaders move beyond vague ethical guidelines into actionable governance, compliance tracking, and audit-ready reporting.
videos.jargon_explained: AI Governance Framework is a structured operating model defining who owns AI decisions, what policies govern model usage, and how algorithmic accountability is documented for regulators.
vendor_questions: Ask the person responsible for governance whether your firm has an up-to-date AI system inventory covering all software with built-in generative features.
Ask your vendors to provide third-party SOC 2 Type II or ISO 42001 compliance certificates for any AI-enabled tools they deliver.

playlists.name: Phase 1: Agentic AI Foundations
playlists.subtitle: The Paradigm Shift from Passive Chatbots to Autonomous Agents
playlists.description: Foundational syllabus covering the mechanics of Large Language Models, the distinction between machine learning and generative AI, and the transition toward goal-driven Agentic AI.
playlists.vendor_note: Even medium enterprises have multi-departmental interactions and confidentiality standards. Ask your managed service provider (MSP) or cloud vendors what foundational model hosting options they support.

videos.title: AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Generative AI Explained
videos.summary: Deconstructs the layered hierarchy of artificial intelligence, supervised machine learning, neural networks, and modern generative models.
videos.jargon_explained: Machine Learning is an AI term for computer algorithms that learn patterns from historical data rather than following hardcoded rules.
vendor_questions: Ask the person responsible for your IT what existing data sets are already structured and ready for internal knowledge retrieval.
Ask your managed service provider (MSP) which AI capabilities are already built into your existing enterprise software licenses.

videos.title: AI vs Machine Learning
videos.summary: Clarifies common enterprise misconceptions between rule-based automation, statistical machine learning, and generative reasoning.
videos.jargon_explained: Generative AI is an AI term for models that synthesize new content (such as legal summaries, client briefs, or code) rather than just predicting numbers or classifying categories.
vendor_questions: Ask your software vendors whether their 'AI-powered' tools rely on standard deterministic algorithms or generative language models.

videos.title: How Large Language Models Work
videos.summary: Explains tokenization, attention mechanisms, and probability distributions that power foundational models such as those offered by IBM, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, or Anthropic.
videos.jargon_explained: Context Window is an AI term for the maximum amount of text and data a model can read and remember in a single interaction, which means that exceeding this limit causes the model to truncate or forget earlier details.
vendor_questions: Ask your cloud hosting partner where client data is processed and whether your data is ever used to retrain the vendor's foundation models.

videos.title: Generative vs Agentic AI: Shaping the Future of AI Collaboration
videos.summary: Covers the critical evolution from passive prompt-and-response chatbots to proactive, multi-step Agentic AI that plans, executes tools, and reviews its own output.
videos.jargon_explained: Agentic AI is an AI term for systems designed with autonomy—capable of breaking a business goal down into sub-tasks, choosing the right digital tools, and self-correcting along the way.
vendor_questions: Ask your technology advisors which repetitive, multi-step workflows in your firm (such as audit preparation or market research) are prime candidates for agentic automation.

playlists.name: Phase 2: Agentic AI Developer Lab
playlists.subtitle: Harnesses, Context Engineering, Spec-Driven Development & Data Layers
playlists.description: Hands-on architectural tutorials detailing how autonomous agents are structured, how context is injected, and why rigorous specification beats unstructured 'vibe coding'.
playlists.vendor_note: Even medium enterprises have complex departmental handoffs. Modern agentic stacks leverage frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or Semantic Kernel, connected to data layers such as Astra DB, Pinecone, or PostgreSQL pgvector.

videos.title: The 7 Skills You Need to Build AI Agents
videos.summary: A core breakdown of the 7 fundamental disciplines required to develop reliable enterprise AI agents.
videos.jargon_explained: Agentic Harness is a software engineering term for the runtime framework that wraps around an AI model to equip it with external tools, state memory, and decision guardrails.
vendor_questions: Ask your implementation partner what framework they use to orchestrate autonomous agents across your firm's applications.

videos.title: AI Model vs Agentic Harness: What Actually Drives AI
videos.summary: Why the raw foundation model is just the engine, while the agentic harness provides the steering wheel, brakes, memory, and tool connections.
videos.jargon_explained: Deterministic vs Probabilistic is a systems term: deterministic code produces the exact same outcome every time (like a calculator), while probabilistic models generate answers based on statistical likelihoods.
vendor_questions: Ask your solution vendors how they ensure deterministic checks and approval gates prevent probabilistic errors in mission-critical client reports.

videos.title: Skills vs MCP vs RAG vs Memory: What AI Agents Need to Know
videos.summary: Compares tool calling, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and working memory for autonomous agents.
videos.jargon_explained: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open industry standard that allows AI agents to securely connect to diverse data sources, business tools, and internal company drives.
vendor_questions: Ask your managed service provider if your enterprise tools support standardized protocol integrations such as MCP or secure REST APIs.

videos.title: What Is Context Engineering? Why It Matters for AI Agents
videos.summary: Explains how to systematically curate, filter, and structure dynamic information presented to an AI model rather than blindly stuffing prompts.
videos.jargon_explained: Context Engineering is an AI term for curating only the exact relevant data, business guidelines, and schema rules an agent needs at any given step, which means that tokens are conserved and hallucinations are minimized.
vendor_questions: Ask the person responsible for your IT architecture how client engagement documents are indexed and filtered before being sent to an LLM.

videos.title: How Context Engineering Improves AI Coding Agents
videos.summary: Demonstrates practical techniques to feed agents relevant architectural guidelines, unit tests, and style guides to build production-grade software.
videos.jargon_explained: Hallucination is an AI term for when an AI model outputs factually incorrect or invented statements with high confidence, which means that verification mechanisms are mandatory.
vendor_questions: Ask your external software contractors what automated testing and linting protocols are enforced when using AI coding assistants.

videos.title: Stop Vibe Coding: Build Better Apps with Spec Kit
videos.summary: Contrasts haphazard prompt-and-pray development ('vibe coding') with rigorous, specification-driven software engineering.
videos.jargon_explained: Vibe Coding is an informal industry term for asking an AI to write code without clear requirements or architecture plans, which means that the resulting software is often brittle and unmaintainable.
vendor_questions: Ask the person responsible for IT delivery to ensure every AI-assisted initiative starts with written technical specifications and sign-offs.

videos.title: Agentic Coding + Planning: Why Specs Matter More Than Code
videos.summary: Explains how multi-agent planning loops use structured requirements to draft plans, execute code, and autonomously verify outputs against acceptance criteria.
videos.jargon_explained: Planning Phase is an AI engineering term where an agent drafts a step-by-step roadmap for human review before executing any irreversible modifications or code changes.
vendor_questions: Ask your vendors if their AI tools support human-in-the-loop review steps before actions are finalized.

videos.title: What Is RAD? Why It Matters in the Age of AI Coding
videos.summary: Revitalizes Rapid Application Development (RAD) principles, emphasizing prototyping, iterative user feedback, and fast software release cycles with AI assistance.
videos.jargon_explained: RAD (Rapid Application Development) is a software methodology term focusing on building working prototypes quickly and iterating with end-users rather than spending months in theoretical design.
vendor_questions: Ask your digital transformation leads how fast prototypes can be piloted with trusted internal user groups.

videos.title: Build an Agentic Data Layer with Astra DB Using Python
videos.summary: Walks through establishing a scalable vector database foundation for autonomous agents. DataStax Astra DB is demonstrated alongside discussions of alternatives such as Pinecone, Milvus, or PostgreSQL with pgvector.
videos.jargon_explained: Vector Database is an AI term for a database optimized to store semantic meanings (vectors) rather than exact text matches, which means that agents can perform conceptual searches across thousands of PDF client files.
vendor_questions: Ask your managed database provider which vector indexing engines (such as pgvector, Pinecone, or Astra DB) best match your company's data compliance boundaries.

playlists.name: Phase 3: Expert Agentic AI Consultant
playlists.subtitle: Security, OWASP Top 10, Containment Breaches & Enterprise Risk Governance
playlists.target_role: Managing Partners, Risk Officers & Senior Advisors
playlists.description: Senior advisory and risk governance framework. Covers deterministic rules versus autonomous agents, synthetic data degradation, OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, and containment isolation.
playlists.vendor_note: Professional services firms handle confidential client records. Even medium enterprises face serious liabilities if agents operate without boundaries. Ask the person responsible for IT compliance and your managed service provider to implement strict vendor assurance protocols.

videos.title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?
videos.summary: Strategic evaluation of where deterministic business rule engines must be maintained (e.g. legal compliance, fee calculations) versus where probabilistic AI agents excel.
videos.jargon_explained: Business Rules Engine is a business process automation term for software that executes strict, immutable 'if-then' policies that cannot deviate or make creative guesses.
vendor_questions: Ask your compliance officer which client decisions must legally remain bound by rigid business rules rather than probabilistic AI models.

videos.title: What Is AI Model Collapse? Why AI Could Forget Reality
videos.summary: Examines the systemic risk when AI models are trained on recursive, synthetic content generated by earlier models, resulting in degraded quality and distorted factual reality.
videos.jargon_explained: Model Collapse is an AI term for a degenerative process where an AI model trained repeatedly on AI-generated data begins losing variety and real-world accuracy over generations.
vendor_questions: Ask your data vendors to disclose the provenance and authenticity of any third-party training data sets they sell or license to your firm.

videos.title: The OWASP LLM Top 10: Emerging Vulnerabilities in Enterprise AI
videos.summary: Walkthrough of the OWASP (Open Web Application Security Project) Top 10 risks for Large Language Models and autonomous agentic workflows.
videos.jargon_explained: Blast Radius is a cybersecurity and resilience term for the total potential damage or spread across your enterprise if an autonomous AI agent makes an erroneous decision or executes an unauthorized action.
vendor_questions: Ask the person responsible for IT security if your enterprise AI deployments are regularly audited against the OWASP LLM Top 10 checklist.
Ask your managed service provider (MSP) what logging and real-time monitoring are in place for outbound API calls made by AI tools.

videos.title: Containment Breaches & Autonomous Browser Vulnerabilities
videos.summary: Analyzes real-world incidents where AI models broke out of simulation environments, and details vulnerabilities in browser-operating agents.
videos.jargon_explained: Containment Breach is a cybersecurity term for an event where an AI program accesses file directories, internal network boundaries, or system resources beyond its restricted sandbox.
vendor_questions: Ask your software vendors whether autonomous browser agents operate inside isolated, temporary cloud containers or directly on employee workstations.

videos.title: Open-Weight Models, Context Bombing & Defense Strategies
videos.summary: Deep dive into open-weight models (such as Meta Llama, Mistral, or GLM), context bombing techniques, and social engineering vectors targeting AI professionals.
videos.jargon_explained: Context Bombing is a cybersecurity term for flooding an AI's input window with hidden, deceptive text designed to confuse its reasoning or trigger secret instructions.
vendor_questions: Ask your managed IT provider what input sanitization and prompt firewalls are active to strip out hidden malicious commands from client-submitted documents.

videos.title: AI Containment Boundaries & Enterprise Defense Controls
videos.summary: Architectural principles for constructing air-gapped sandboxes, role-based tool restrictions, and zero-trust permissions for autonomous agents.
videos.jargon_explained: Zero-Trust Architecture is a cybersecurity term meaning that no user, device, or autonomous agent is automatically trusted; every single action or data query must be verified before execution.
vendor_questions: Ask the person responsible for your cloud tenant to ensure AI agents are provisioned with least-privilege read-only permissions by default.

videos.title: Sandbox Breaches, EU AI Transparency Regulations & Cost Economics
videos.summary: Synthesizes security breaches with emerging regulatory frameworks (such as the EU AI Act) and the economic cost models of running frontier vs cost-optimized open-weight models.
videos.jargon_explained: EU AI Act Compliance is a regulatory term for statutory legal requirements requiring enterprises to disclose AI usage, audit high-risk decision systems, and ensure human oversight.
vendor_questions: Ask your legal counsel and managed IT partner what formal disclosure statements are required before delivering AI-assisted advice to your clients.
